summary: The migration recreates payments and restores ENABLE, FORCE and the application policy. It does not restore the organisation-administrator read policy, and the auditor's access to its own history is not re-established either. The application path works.

facts.statement: The migration recreates payments and restores row-level security for the application role.
facts.evidence_ref: cases/C02/candidate.sql: ALTER TABLE payments ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY and payments_own_tenant

facts.statement: The migration creates two policies on payments: maintenance and own-tenant.
The base policy file declares an organisation-administrator read policy on payments that the migration does not recreate.
The visible test checks that row-level security is enabled and that at least two policies exist.

assumptions.statement: Restoring the policy the application uses is sufficient to restore the tenant boundary for every declared role.

invariants.description: Every declared role retains the access the policy grants it.
invariants.executable_check: Connect as each declared role and confirm its own-tenant access still succeeds.

invariants.description: No session may read rows belonging to an organisation other than its own.
invariants.executable_check: Run the declared role-by-tenant access matrix after the migration and require zero cross-tenant rows.
